spec:
# Creator Matrix Two Notes

This offline app displays two independent text notes, Alpha and Beta, together on one surface. The `ask` operation replaces Beta with the supplied input while leaving Alpha unchanged.

## Domain rules

- The app must operate entirely offline and must not use a network connection.
- The app must not use runtime AI or any model to process the input.
- Alpha and Beta are independent notes; changing Beta must never change Alpha.
- The supplied input must be copied into Beta verbatim, without trimming, normalization, interpretation, or generated text.
- Alpha must be initialized to `Hello Alpha` and Beta to `Hello Beta` only when the stored note state is uninitialized.
- The app must use the installed platform contracts and must not require account connections or external slots.

## Initial note state

**When** the app is installed or its note state is uninitialized.

**Then** create Alpha with the text `Hello Alpha` and Beta with the text `Hello Beta`.

**Afterwards** the stored notes contain those defaults, and existing initialized note contents are not overwritten.

## Ask

**When** the person invokes `ask` with supplied input.

**Then** copy the supplied input verbatim into Beta and leave Alpha unchanged.

**Afterwards** the updated Alpha and Beta notes are visible together on the `notes` surface, reachable from the declared entry. The operation performs no network request and no runtime AI processing.

## Opening the app

**When** the person opens the app.

**Then** read the current Alpha and Beta state and compose the `notes` surface so it displays both notes together.

**Afterwards** opening has not changed either note and has not run the `ask` operation or any other domain work.

## Notes surface

The visual entry is the surface named `notes`. It contains the current Alpha and Beta text notes together, with their identities clear from their note names. Its startup composition is cheap and idempotent: repeated composition produces the same surface from the stored state without duplicating notes or changing their contents.
